title: ci: bump the agent review to wachiman v1.4.0
body:
## What

Moves the agent review pin from `niway-dev/wachiman@v1.3.0` to [`v1.4.0`](https://github.com/niway-dev/wachiman/releases/tag/v1.4.0), and records the bump in ADR 0028's "reviews also run on every push" amendment.

## Why

`main` already lists `synchronize` (ADR 0028, amendment of 2026-11-01), but it still ran v1.3.0, which predates the push mode. v1.4.0 is the release built for it:

- a rebase with no content change only moves the marker and makes no model call;
- merging the base branch into a PR reviews none of the base's files;
- reasoning effort is an explicit input, printed in every footer (default `high`, unchanged here);
- each call is capped at 40 agent turns and 900 s wall clock;
- each batch gets the other call sites of the symbols the diff newly calls;
- findings carry a confidence, enforced in code.

The caller keeps `model: claude-opus-5-5` and the default budgets ($0.75 per batch, $3 per review). No new `with:` inputs: `review_on_push` defaults to `true`.

Still open (ADR 0028 now says so): a rebase that changes content reviews again, and there is no per-PR spending limit.

## How to test it yourself

1. This PR's own "Agent review" run should use v1.4.0: the review comment footer names the effort (`high`) and the model (Opus 5.5).
2. Push one more small commit to this branch: a new run should review only that commit, not the whole PR.
3. Optional: rebase this branch on `main` without changing content and force-push; the run should end without a model call (no new findings, near-zero cost in the log).
4. After merge, compare on the next feature PRs: findings per push, cost per run (from the run log), and how many findings land on fix commits.
